We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1.

We have template 647549 which breaks amide to give an aniline and a carboxylic acid? Actually retro: product is amide, reactants are O-alkyl ester? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: [O;D1;H0:2]=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[NH;D2;+0:8]-[c:9])-[c:3]1:[#7;a:4]:[#7;a:5]:[#7;a:6]:[c:7]:1>> O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[c:3]1... . So forward reaction is amide formation from carboxylic acid (or ester?) Actually forward: O-alkyl? The reactants are O-alkyl? The left side of >> is product (amide). Right side are O-alkyl? The template indicates breaking amide to give carboxylic acid (O-CO) and an aniline? So applying retro will give two fragments: a carboxylic acid (or ester) and an aniline.

Our target has an amide linking an aniline (the phenoxy ring) to a heterocycle (c2nnn...). So step 1 could be disconnection of amide to give aniline (the anisole phenyl with NH) and the heterocycle carboxylic acid (or maybe acid chloride). So we need a precursor: aniline part: COc1cccc(NH) c1? Actually target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)...) So the aniline is COc1cccc(NH-CO...). So the fragment after breaking amide: aniline with COc1cccc(NH) c1 (i.e., anisidine). That's 4-methoxy-aniline? Actually COc1cccc(NH) c1 is anisidine (para? not sure). The other fragment is the heterocycle with carboxylic acid: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N attached to carbonyl.

Thus step 1: amide disconnection using template 647549.

Now we need further disconnections to reach simple precursors in total 3 steps.

The heterocycle is a 1,2,4-triazine? Actually nnn ring. It has an N attached to CH2-aryl (phenyl with side chain CN4...). Also an exocyclic NH (c2nnn(... )c2N). So we could break the C-N bond linking the heterocycle to the aryl side chain via SN2? The side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached via CH2 to heterocycle nitrogen? Actually pattern: nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3) meaning the heterocycle nitrogen attached to CH2-aryl. So we could disconnect that via SN2: the CH2 attached to heterocycle nitrogen could be formed by nucleophilic substitution of a halide on the aryl side chain with the heterocycle nitrogen as nucleophile? Actually forward SN2: nucleophile attacks electrophilic carbon bearing leaving group (halide). So retro SN2 would break C-N bond to give halide on the carbon and free heterocycle nitrogen (as amine). So we need a template for SN2 on alkyl halide with nitrogen nucleophile. Search for functional_groups_broken ["alkyl halide"] gave template 1914393 which is a SN2 on benzyl halide with amine? It shows Cl-CH2-aryl + amine -> CH2-aryl-N. That matches our side chain: we have CH2 attached to heterocycle N. So we can use that.

Thus step 2: disconnection of CH2-aryl bond to give heterocycle with NH (maybe as NH) and a benzyl chloride (or bromide) on the aryl ring.

The aryl side chain is phenyl with substituent CN4CC(F)C4 (i.e., a side chain containing a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-membered? It's a N-azetidine with fluorine. So the aryl ring has a substituent CH2-N4... So the benzyl chloride would be on the same carbon that attaches to heterocycle? Actually the CH2 is attached to heterocycle N and to phenyl ring (benzyl). So the benzyl chloride precursor would be a phenyl-CH2-Cl (para? not important). The phenyl also has a substituent CN4CC(F)C4 (i.e., a side chain with a tertiary amine). So we need that substituent present.

Thus step 2 yields two fragments: heterocycle with NH (still attached to exocyclic NH) and benzyl chloride (aryl-CH2-Cl) with the side chain.

Now step 3: we need to construct the heterocycle (triazine) and the side chain maybe via Friedel-Crafts acylation? The guidance mentions Friedel-Crafts acylation to introduce acyl onto aromatic ring. Our heterocycle is attached to carbonyl (amide) already handled. The heterocycle itself maybe formed via cyclization from a precursor like a hydrazine? But we have limited steps (3 total). Perhaps we can consider that the heterocycle fragment (c2nnn(... )c2N) could be derived from a simple precursor via a substitution (e.g., formation of triazine from a diacylhydrazine). However maybe we can use a template that breaks the N-N bond (functional group broken: azo?). Search for functional_groups_broken ["azo"]? Let's try.
